text:
eva: Heads-up: nightly eval flagged a big uptick in degenerate / repetitive generations after we onboarded model v5b last night. Failing rate jumped from 2.1% -> 9.8% on the prompt suite. :warning:
nightly-bot: nightly-run v5b-2026-03-19 finished. metrics: perplexity +0.4, degenerate_rate 9.8% (baseline 2.1%). artifacts: s3://redwood-nightly/v5b/2026-03-19/
ajay: Thanks, eva. Can you paste a couple of example prompts + outputs?
eva: Yup, two short ones below (redacted). Note repeating tail tokens and early stop not triggering.
```
PROMPT: "Summarize the meeting: goals, blockers, next steps"
EXPECTED: short bulleted summary
OUTPUT: "Summary: goals: goals: goals: goals: goals..." (repeats ~120 tokens)
```
```
PROMPT: "Write a 3-paragraph explainer on feature rollout"
OUTPUT: "Paragraph 1... Paragraph 1... Paragraph 1..." repeated blocks
```
maria: Hmm. Any change in tokenization mapping between v5a -> v5b? We did swap to merged-bpe-2026 token table last week.
kevin: Also note we changed the default quantization profile to q4_1 in the model build (smaller footprint). Could be rounding interacting with attention scaling.
eva: I ran a quick diff on tokenized lengths for the prompt suite. For ~12% of prompts v5b tokenizes 1-3 tokens longer compared to v5a. But the degenerate cases aren't perfectly correlated with length delta.
ajay: Could be KV cache misalignment when token ids shift. If tokenizer mapping changes, cached prefix keys might not align and attention could see weird repeats. Any evidence in server logs?
kevin: Pulling recent inference logs now. (snippet)
```
[2026-03-19T02:11:03Z] req=abcd model=v5b weights=sha256:9f3a... quant=q4_1 seq=512 produced_repeat=1
[2026-03-19T02:11:03Z] kv_cache_hit=false prefix_hash=0x7f12
```
kevin: I see several requests with kv_cache_hit=false where previously they'd hit. That supports cache mismatch theory.
maria: If the tokenizer changed, prefix hashes used in the cache key would differ and cause more cold-start decoding leading to repetition patterns (we saw similar once with v3 migration).
eva: I repro locally with the nightly harness by forcing cache usage vs cold start. When I clear cache every prompt, degenerate rate goes up but not as high as nightly.
ajay: Two-pronged triage plan: 1) Reproduce in an isolated env with v5a/v5b using identical tokenizers and track token ids; 2) Run AB where v5b uses fallback to v5a tokenizer mapping at serving time to see if degens drop.
kevin: I'll deploy a hotfix: keep v5b weights but load legacy-tokenizer mapping at runtime (cheap config flip) and run the failing prompt subset. If that fixes it, we know tokenizer delta is primary.
maria: Also let's snapshot quant profiles: run v5b with q4_0 + legacy tokenizer to rule out quant interaction.
eva: I've opened an eval issue: https://redwood/issue/ML-1428 with sample failed outputs, seed, and harness args. Adding repro instructions and a minimal script.
ajay: Good. Assign to kevin+eva. ETA for first repro run?
kevin: Will run AB and post results within 2 hours.
eva: I'll start token-id diffs for the full prompt suite and attach CSV to the issue.
kevin: Quick note: if cache mismatch is true, we may also see latency variance spikes. I'll check CDN traces.
nightly-bot: added artifact s3://redwood-nightly/v5b/2026-03-19/reports/degen_examples.json to thread.
maria: Thanks all — if kv/cache is culprit we should revert tokenizer promotion until we have migration hooks for prefix-preserving mappings. :+1:
eva: Agreed. For now, flagging Dedicated hosts that serve v5b to avoid rollout. I'll send a short post in #eng-runtime to hold canary.
kevin: Results: with legacy tokenizer mapping applied, degenerate_rate on the failing subset drops from 78% -> 3.5%. Pushing these logs to the issue. Looks decisive for tokenizer mismatch.
ajay: Perfect. Next steps: revert tokenizer change in the model packaging pipeline, add tokenization compatibility test in nightly harness, and gate tokenizer promotions behind a rollout with KV-cache-aware validation.
maria: I'll add a checklist to the onboarding playbook.
eva: Closing the triage for now; leaving the issue open for packaging + release notes. Thanks everyone. :tada:
